description: The pie chart represents the distribution of curated mathematical problems across subject areas and educational levels, showing 12 labeled categories with percentages and counts annotated outside the slices via leader lines (no separate legend is shown, and no slice appears exploded or otherwise emphasized). The slices are: “Algebra – Olympiad-level” in dark blue at about 21.19% (82); “Algebra – High School” in light pink/salmon at about 17.83% (69); “Pre-Calculus – High School” in brown at about 14.21% (55); “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” in light green at about 9.56% (37); “Geometry – Olympiad-level” in light orange/peach at about 6.46% (25); “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” in magenta/pink at about 6.46% (25); “Calculus and Analysis – University-level” in gray at about 6.20% (24); “Probability – University-level” in teal at about 5.43% (21); “Statistics – University-level” in light blue/cyan at about 4.39% (17); “Differential Equations – University-level” in yellow-green at about 3.62% (14); “Geometry – High School” in light lavender at about 3.62% (14); and “Number Theory – Olympiad-level” in very light gray at about 1.03% (4). The segments appear arranged around the circle without an obvious strictly descending or ascending size order.
